Vinci SA Unveils Modular Bridge System for Polish Infrastructure Market

Vinci SA, a leading player in Poland’s Engineering & Construction sector, has announced the launch of its new modular bridge system, designed to accelerate transport infrastructure upgrades across the country. The product, named VinciSpan, was officially presented at a press conference in Warsaw on Thursday.

VinciSpan is a prefabricated steel and concrete bridge solution aimed at municipalities and construction firms seeking faster, cost-effective options for replacing or expanding existing crossings. According to Vinci SA, the system reduces installation time by up to 40% compared to traditional bridge construction methods and offers a lifespan of over 50 years.

“Our goal with VinciSpan is to address Poland’s urgent need for modern, resilient infrastructure,” said Anna Kowalczyk, General Manager of Vinci SA Poland. “With significant investments planned for road and rail networks in the coming years, this technology allows us to deliver high-quality solutions more quickly and efficiently.”

The launch comes as Poland continues to invest heavily in its transport networks, with government figures showing a planned allocation of PLN 32 billion for road modernization in the 2024-2027 period. Industry analysts suggest that modular systems like VinciSpan are well-suited to meet the demand for rapid project delivery, especially in rural and semi-urban areas where construction windows are limited.

“The Polish construction sector is under increasing pressure to deliver projects on tight schedules,” said Marek Zielinski, infrastructure analyst at the Warsaw Institute for Economic Development. “Products that offer both speed and durability, such as VinciSpan, are likely to see strong uptake, particularly as local authorities seek to minimize disruption to traffic and communities.”

Vinci SA stated that VinciSpan has already undergone pilot installations in the Mazovia and Lesser Poland provinces, where local officials reported positive feedback regarding installation speed and environmental impact. The company further noted that the system is compatible with a variety of span lengths and load requirements, making it suitable for both road and rail applications.

The Polish Association of Civil Engineers welcomed the launch, with Vice President Tomasz Borowski commenting, “Innovations like VinciSpan will help Poland meet its infrastructure goals and improve safety for all users.”

Vinci SA expects to begin full-scale commercial deliveries of VinciSpan in the third quarter of 2024 and is in discussions with several regional contractors, including BialTech and PolConstruct, regarding upcoming bridge replacement projects.
